summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, a general-availability frontier model with new capability-based safeguards, alongside Claude Mythos 5, a less-restricted variant for trusted cybersecurity and biology partners, both priced below the prior Mythos Preview model.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states the new model is state-of-the-art on nearly all benchmarks and exceeds any previously generally available Claude model.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5’s capabilities exceed those of any model we’ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability

mechanisms.reason: The new frontier-class models are priced at less than half the cost per token of the prior Mythos Preview model.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are being offered at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens—less than half the price of Claude Mythos Preview.

mechanisms.reason: The model is described as enabling longer autonomous agentic work and handing increasingly ambitious tasks to agents across the software lifecycle.
mechanisms.quote: a future where developers can hand increasingly ambitious work to agents and trust the results across the software lifecycle

mechanisms.reason: The model sustains focus and persistent memory across millions of tokens in long-running tasks, increasing context and memory demands per session.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 stays focused across millions of tokens in long-running tasks and improves its outputs using its own notes.

mechanisms.reason: The model is capable of extended, largely autonomous multi-day research sessions, implying substantially higher token/inference volume per task.
mechanisms.quote: Mythos 5 conducted novel genomics research in over a week of largely autonomous work.

notable_reason: A frontier model release with a disclosed capability jump and a steep per-token price cut is directly relevant to inference economics and agentic workload growth.
